issues.description: lora_config.is_registered mutation is not thread-safe and races under concurrent first-use
issues.detail: TritonLoraConfig is a shared mutable dataclass stored in TritonModelMetadata.lora_configs. _create_trtllm_generate_request reads is_registered, loads weights, and sets is_registered=True without any synchronization. Under concurrent first-use of the same LoRA (the normal case the moment two requests arrive), multiple coroutines/threads will all observe is_registered=False, all load the .npy files from disk, all attach lora_weights/lora_config to their requests, and then race on assignment. The invariant 'first request carries weights, subsequent requests carry only task_id' is therefore not maintained. The fix is either an asyncio.Lock per TritonLoraConfig with a check-after-acquire, or always sending weights+config (idempotent in TRT-LLM's LoRA cache) and dropping is_registered entirely. The latter is the literate choice: it removes the invariant rather than guarding it.

issues.description: lora_task_id is assigned per-call to _parse_lora_configs, not stably across server lifetime
issues.detail: lora_task_id starts at 1 inside _parse_lora_configs and increments per LoRA. _parse_lora_configs is called from _get_model_metadata, which may be invoked more than once (model reload, metadata refresh). On a second call the same LoRA name can be assigned a different task_id while the TRT-LLM backend still holds the old task_id in its cache; worse, two different LoRAs across model-repo entries can collide on the same small integer because the counter resets per call within one repo walk and there is no global registry. The invariant 'name -> task_id is a stable bijection for the life of the cache' is not stated and not maintained. State the invariant and enforce it with a server-scoped counter or hash-derived id.

issues.description: O(L) linear scans over lora_configs replace what was O(1) membership in lora_names
issues.detail: The previous code did 'lora_name in metadata.lora_names' against a list (already linear but small). The new code does two list comprehensions in the hot validation path ('lora_name not in [c.name for c in metadata.lora_configs]') in both _validate_chat_request and _validate_completion_request, and a third linear scan in _get_lora_config on every request. Asymptotically this is O(L) per request where L is the number of LoRAs; practically L is small so this is not yet hot. Still, the data structure for 'lookup LoRA config by name' is a dict, not a list. Choose the data structure: store lora_configs as Dict[str, TritonLoraConfig] (or augment with a name->config index) and the three call sites collapse to a single dict.get. This is the Pike/Knuth point — the algorithm is fine, the structure is paying interest.

issues.description: .npy files are re-read from disk on every first-use without caching the parsed arrays
issues.detail: _create_trtllm_generate_request calls np.load on model.lora_weights.npy and model.lora_config.npy inside the request hot path. Even with is_registered short-circuiting subsequent calls, the *first* request pays a synchronous blocking file read inside an async coroutine, and under the race above it pays it N times. The literate solution is to load and cache the numpy arrays once at _parse_lora_configs time (when we already verified the files exist) and attach them to TritonLoraConfig as Optional[np.ndarray] fields. That also removes the synchronous I/O from the async path, which is a separate correctness concern (blocking the event loop).

issues.description: lora_config_path variable is shadowed inside the loop, breaking the loop's stated meaning
issues.detail: Around line 658 lora_config_path is bound to '<version>/multi_lora.json'. Inside the per-LoRA loop it is rebound to os.path.join(lora_path, 'model.lora_config.npy'). On the next iteration of the outer repo_paths loop, or on a subsequent call, the reader cannot tell which lora_config_path is in scope without tracing rebindings. This is exactly the readability defect literate programming exists to prevent. Rename to lora_weights_file_path and lora_config_file_path (or lora_npy_config_path) and the bug class — and the reader's confusion — both disappear.

issues.description: Bare 'except Exception' in _parse_lora_configs swallows real errors and returns None
issues.detail: The outer try around json.load now also wraps the per-LoRA file existence checks (which raise ServerError, re-raised correctly) plus everything else. Any unrelated exception — a typo in the LoRA dict producing a TypeError, a permission error, an OSError on a network mount — is caught, traceback printed to stdout, and the function returns None. The caller then treats the model as having no LoRA support at all, silently. The invariant 'multi_lora.json is present and parseable implies LoRA support is configured' is contradicted by the catch-all. Narrow the except to JSONDecodeError / OSError, or let it propagate as ServerError with context.

Line ~681 prints the backend on every LoRA entry during metadata parsing. This is debug residue. It will appear in production logs at startup for every model x every LoRA. Remove it, or move it once before the loop with proper logging.

issues.description: traceback.print added to fastapi routers and to _parse_lora_configs uses print, not the logger
issues.detail: chat.py, completions.py, embeddings.py each gain 'print(traceback.format_exc())' on ServerError and Exception branches, and _parse_lora_configs does the same. This is fine for debugging but is unstructured stdout output that bypasses whatever logging configuration the frontend uses. Route through logging.exception with a stable logger name so operators can filter and so log aggregation captures level/timestamp consistently.

issues.description: Return type annotation of _parse_lora_configs is stale (says List[tuple[str, str]])
issues.detail: Signature reads '-> None | List[tuple[str, str]]' but the function returns List[TritonLoraConfig]. The annotation is wrong; mypy / a careful reader is misled. Update to 'Optional[List[TritonLoraConfig]]'. Small fix, but precisely the kind of thing literate programming refuses to let slide — the type is part of the explanation.

issues.description: _get_lora_config will NoneType-deref when model_name is not in self.model_metadata
issues.detail: self.model_metadata.get(model_name) returns None silently; the next line dereferences model_metadata.lora_configs. The 'if lora_name is None' branch saves the common case but a caller passing an unknown model_name with a lora_name will get AttributeError instead of a ClientError. State the invariant ('caller has already validated model_name exists') and assert it, or handle the miss explicitly with a ClientError. Right now neither holds.

issues.description: TritonLoraConfig.is_registered defaults to Optional[bool]=False — the Optional is misleading
issues.detail: is_registered is declared Optional[bool] = False but is only ever read/written as a plain bool (and used in 'if not lora_config.is_registered'). None would be a third state with no defined meaning. Drop the Optional. Small thing; matters because the type tells the reader what states are reachable.

review.summary: UNDER-AUDITED and WRONG-DATA-STRUCTURE. The feature works in the happy-path single-request case but the LoRA-registration state machine has not had its invariants stated, and once stated they do not hold under concurrency or model reload. Two P0s: the is_registered flag is a shared mutable boolean mutated from async request handlers without a lock (concurrent first-use races, blocking np.load on the event loop), and lora_task_id is assigned per parse-call rather than per server-lifetime so reloads can reassign ids the backend cache still maps to old weights. The data structure for lora lookups is also wrong: a list of dataclasses where a Dict[str, TritonLoraConfig] would make every request-path lookup O(1) and remove three list-comprehension scans. Code-audit findings are mostly readability and dead-debug residue (shadowed lora_config_path, stray prints, stale return annotation, bare except swallowing real errors). State the invariants, switch the lookup structure, cache the .npy arrays at parse time, and the algorithm becomes RIGOROUS.
